steps.label: "It's secretly 0 or 1, we just don't know which"
steps.sub: A classical probabilistic mixture — like a spinning coin before it lands

steps.label: The uncertainty lives in your head, not the qubit
steps.sub: A definite, pre-existing value is assumed to already be there

steps.label: This picture makes a testable prediction
steps.sub: Two operations in a row should just be two independent draws

steps.label: Quantum mechanics violates that prediction, every time
steps.sub: And one gate is all it takes to show it

code:
H|0> = |+>
H|+> = |0>   (exact, every time — H.H = I)

classical mixture prediction:
two 50/50 steps -> a spread of outcomes

actual result: 100% certain return to |0>
caption: A classical hidden-variable mixture has no mechanism to make two 50/50 steps cancel into one certain outcome — but that's exactly what H·H=I does.

steps.label: Amplitudes add together before you square them
steps.sub: If they point the same way, constructive interference — reinforce

steps.label: If they point opposite ways, destructive interference
steps.sub: They cancel, even all the way to zero

steps.label: Plain probabilities can never do this
steps.sub: Probabilities are non-negative — they only add, never cancel

steps.label: This is why physicists trust superposition is real
steps.sub: Not a stand-in for ignorance — amplitudes genuinely cancel

steps.label: Circuits are engineered sequences of gates
steps.sub: Designed to interfere wrong answers toward zero

steps.label: And interfere the correct answer toward certainty
steps.sub: Constructive reinforcement on the right amplitude

steps.label: If superposition were just hidden ignorance...
steps.sub: There'd be nothing to interfere, and no advantage over flipping coins

subtitle: How amplitudes become the probabilities you actually observe.
